# Mahjong Garden

A quiet, dependency-free mahjong solitaire game with **60 unique levels**, CSS 3D tiles, six illustrated chapter environments, traditional/animal/emoji tile collections, and a personal tile studio.

[Play Mahjong Garden](https://grab-lead-8328.onpagelove.com/) · [Public source](https://github.com/wesley83/mahjong-garden)

## Play

Match identical free tiles. A tile must have no tile directly above it and an open left or right side. Clear the board to finish. Flowers and winds use exact-symbol matching. Every initial deal and reshuffle has a verified solution; your choices can still lead to a dead end. Undo, hints, reshuffle and restart are always available.

All 60 levels are open from the beginning. Earn one star for completion, two without reshuffles, and three without either hints or reshuffles. Undo has no added penalty and keeps the hint/reshuffle use already recorded for that attempt. Change tile collections during a run without changing its pairs.

Begin or continue from the title screen. Menu returns to the title without resetting your board. Tile collections, all sixty levels and the personal studio remain available through game menus. Each tile uses front, back and side planes with CSS perspective.

Use mouse/touch, Tab and Enter/Space. Arrow keys move tile focus. **H** reveals a pair; **U** undoes; **Escape** clears selection. A text tile view exposes the same actions. Settings offer larger tiles, reduced motion, background music and match/celebration effects. Music and effects start enabled (35%/65%) after your first interaction. Each has its own switch and volume slider; choices are remembered. Preview celebration plays the level-clear cue. The clock pauses on the title screen, while a dialog is open or the tab is hidden. There is no time limit.

## Shared leaderboard

Open **Leaderboard** from the title, Settings, or the level-clear screen. Choose any of the 60 official gardens to see its top ten, plus your latest acknowledged result when outside ten. Points include the active-time bonus described below. Equal points share competition ranks (1, 1, 3). Previous stars/time results remain in a separate read-only view. Custom studio layouts are practice; changing tile artwork does not change eligibility.

After clearing an official level, type your public name and choose **Save score**. Names accept 1–24 ASCII letters/digits, spaces, period, apostrophe, dash or underscore. The game remembers the last submitted name. A clean clear starts at10,000 base points. Hints deduct ceil(4,000 × hints ÷ original pair count), each reshuffle deducts2,000, and completing always earns at least1,000. Undo does not deduct points or refund assistance; repeated matches cannot earn extra points. Repeated Hint on the same still-highlighted pair has no extra cost. Stars retain their familiar1–3 completion/assistance rules. One immutable entry is accepted per seeded deal; importing the same deal does not create a new result identity. These are casual, client-reported scores, without authoritative anti-cheat or offensive-name moderation. No full save or photos are submitted.

The immutable pending result is committed locally before sending. **Retry saved result** checks the original identity before posting, including after a lost response. Errors retain the pending result. **Remove local retry** removes only that device's retry; an uncertain earlier request may already be public. A failed refresh keeps older confirmed results only for the same selected level. After a new clear with a remembered name, the frozen result queues automatically. Leaderboard name/retry/receipts are separate from portable game backups; clearing site data removes this local convenience state. Retained acceptance IDs are bounded to 100 and cached complete datasets to three editions. Public records remain until owner removal. Large/invalid collections fail explicitly rather than display misleading partial rankings.

## Daily gardens and your own garden

**Daily Garden** gives everyone the same deal, with separate standings and the last30 days available from October28,2026. Days change at midnight UTC. Weekly challenges offer golden tiles, clearing a marked layer, and a compact board. Entering a challenge saves your journey; **Return to your journey** restores its board and time. Challenge scores stay separate from journey totals. The first saved result per public name and challenge is immutable; names are aliases, not accounts.

Each first journey clear earns one seed, including levels already completed. **Restore your garden** lets you spend seeds on lanterns, little bridges and blossom trees across six scenes. Replays and challenges do not create extra seeds. Restoration and daily stamps are local and included in game backup version3; older backups remain supported.

**Share a challenge** in Settings or after a clear copies a link to the exact starting deal. You can copy a result or save a1200×630 result card. Links never contain photos or the current removed tiles. Personal layouts use the studio's file export. Newly freed tiles briefly glow; clearing a nonfinal layer gets a short cue, respecting reduced motion and the effects mixer.

## Your tile studio

Create a layout on an 8 × 6 grid with up to three layers. Use an even number of tiles; upper tiles need support below. Undo/redo layout and image edits, save an unfinished draft, and validate/play a completed layout.

Add 2–36 of your own PNG, JPEG or WebP images (5 MB maximum each). Images are resized locally to at most 160 × 160. Repeated photos carry a small mark number, so visually repeated photos still have distinct matching identities. Export/import a studio file to share a completed layout and its images. The game backup export also preserves unfinished drafts, active runs, preferences and progress.

Progress, settings, drafts and photos are stored in IndexedDB in your browser. Photos are never uploaded by this game. Submitted leaderboard names and results are public shared records on the same Pagelove host. No accounts, analytics or third-party requests. Saves are device/origin specific; clearing browser site data removes them. Export a backup to transfer or keep your work. Quota failures and cross-tab conflicts preserve the previous accepted save and expose retry/export/temporary play. Temporary play does not promise persistence.

## Run and verify

Use Node.js 22 or newer. Production has no package dependencies. Development uses the locked `linkedom` parser. Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 11.25.0 produced the recorded release.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm check
node tools/serve.mjs
# http://127.0.0.1:4173/preview/ — built candidate
# http://127.0.0.1:4173/tests/browser.html — disposable-origin acceptance harness
pnpm gate
```

The baseline compatibility test reads the original released rules from Git commit `0cbfa62865e0e270a5ee967052c25e257199a787`; run the suite from a full Git clone. Set `PORT` to select an unused preview origin. Avoid an origin where an unrelated service worker is installed. For the local browser acceptance harness, open `/tests/browser.html` on a separate disposable preview origin. Its synthetic input/storage tests are explicitly separated from real native pointer/keyboard observations in `audit/`.

Production output lives in ignored `dist/`: an entry page plus immutable, content-addressed release assets. Styles remain editable in style.css/game.css; build freezes their bytes into the entry for deterministic first paint. The game itself remains static; its optional shared board requires the native score document described below. Deploy only the paths in dist/release.json to a static server that serves `.mjs` as JavaScript. A network-only service worker and installation manifest are included; offline reload is not promised.

## Content and architecture

The [development plan](GAME-PLAN.md) follows Pagelove's Web Game Development Handbook edition 2.9.0. [Level HTML](content/levels.html) is the sole authored campaign definition. Every article has a stable identity/revision and readable coordinate-bearing tile elements. `tools/author-levels.mjs` is an explicit authoring operation; ordinary builds validate the existing source instead of silently regenerating it.

`core.mjs` owns validated rules and bounded geometry search; `profile.mjs` shares strict profile/draft validation across restore, writes and tests. `app.mjs` derives gameplay from the HTML library and keeps runtime actions separate from authoring. The live `#studio-source` DOM subtree owns the current editable layout. JSON exports are a versioned interchange format. `storage.mjs` applies revision-checked IndexedDB transactions; unsupported records are retained for recovery rather than erased.

The automated suite verifies all 60 layouts across 12 seeds, legal/illegal actions, deterministic dealing, undo, assistance, bounded search, imports and checkpoint rejection. Browser evidence records layout geometry, storage conflict/quota behavior, studio images and ordinary gameplay. It does not certify enjoyment, full accessibility conformance or untested browser engines/physical phones.

## Pagelove release

The deployment tool is pinned to `grab-lead-8328.onpagelove.com` and its owner DAV host. Run `node tools/deploy-console.mjs` in a terminal with hidden raw stdin. Commands are newline-delimited JSON: `backup` with an owner key, then `deploy`, `quit`. Credentials belong only in hidden stdin; never put them in a script, shell argument, Git, or browser client.

`backup` recursively downloads every resource to ignored `.local/server-backup/<timestamp>` and verifies disk hashes. Updates preserve all existing resources. The original one-time wipe is retained as historical evidence. `deploy` requires matching unit/browser/native receipts, a clean pushed commit and a completed backup. It creates immutable dependencies with create-only conditions, checks public bytes/semantic HTML and MIME types, then promotes the entry with the backed-up strong ETag. It writes a sanitized receipt to `audit/current/deployment.json`.

The original local backup is deliberately excluded from this public repository. To restore it, use the retained manifest to recreate collections and upload the original files through the same authenticated authoring plane; verify readback before promoting the original entry. Conditional entry rollback and retained-release recovery are exercised against an isolated transport fixture; production rollback is not performed. The backup includes previous application policy files, so inspect their intended access before republishing them.

## License and asset provenance

MIT. Traditional tile SVG illustrations, favicon, interface icons and CSS botanical artwork were created for this game. Animal and emoji faces use Unicode characters rendered by the operating system; no emoji font or artwork files are redistributed. Display fonts are system fonts. The original instrumental loop and sound effects are synthesized with Web Audio; no music files or external media are loaded. User-imported images remain the user's responsibility and are absent from the repository and distribution.

The [handbook comparison](audit/HANDBOOK-REVIEW.md) records the nine resolved gap groups, exact-candidate evidence and environment limits. `pnpm check` builds and writes a unit receipt; browser/native receipts require actually executing their respective journeys before `pnpm gate` can pass. Tests never manufacture production acceptance receipts. The gate also checks required asset roles, the 400,000-byte initial gameplay budget and source/artifact hashes. See [asset provenance](assets/ASSETS.md) for optional, reproducible image authoring.


Rapid touch update (1.2.1): surviving tile buttons keep their identity, visible 3D planes accept hits, and touch/pen contacts select independently on release, including secondary fingers. Movement beyond 14 CSS pixels or a browser-canceled gesture does not select a tile. Scroll and pinch zoom remain enabled. The smallest source width is 48 pixels; boards scroll when necessary. Mouse, keyboard and text tiles remain available. `tests/touch.mjs` runs qualified synthetic app input and rendered hit geometry; `audit/touch/` distinguishes this from native desktop and unverified Pixel/Edge behavior.


Audio update1.3.0: game profile/run formats remain1. A separately versioned mixer record is saved atomically with progress, and portable game-backup envelope2 includes both. Older envelope1 backups still import; their game state restores while current mixer preferences remain. First launch of the new mixer enables both channels even if the old default sound flag was false. Later explicit mutes/volumes persist. Reset audio settings also recovers an invalid mixer record without replacing a valid game save. Hidden pages/transitions stop audio; interrupted audio can retry from an eligible gesture or Preview celebration. A completed save restore stays quiet. The build compacts only validated safe campaign data attributes and asserts complete content equality; canonical authored HTML remains quoted/readable. Evidence and scope: audit/audio/.


Leaderboard update 1.4.0: the requested shared service is /mahjong-scores.html, an independent semantic HTML resource with a native POST grant scoped to #scores, exact request grammar, schema cardinality/types and unique run key. No public PUT or DELETE. Source policy: tools/leaderboard-policy.mjs; owner-only hidden-stdin installation/probe: tools/leaderboard-console.mjs. The installer takes a verified full backup, uses disposable fixtures, installs production create-only, checks public enforcement and removes its exact synthetic entry using a strong conditional write while preserving unrelated rows. Ordinary publishing never overwrites this resource. Public shape/unique controls do not establish honest play, total request-rate/quota limits or moderation. Accountless public aliases can be impersonated; they are display names, not identity proof. Owner moderation requires an exact row identity and conditional DAV maintenance; no browser owner key is present. See audit/leaderboard/PLAN.md, server.json and REVIEW.md for contracts, evidence and provider limits. The on-demand module is excluded from the unchanged 400000-byte initial pack budget.


## PWA installation and updates (1.5.0)

Use your browser’s Install app or Add to home screen option when offered. The manifest has192px/512px icons and standalone display. Network is required; neither game nor leaderboard responses are cached by the worker.

The game checks the served release on startup, foreground/online and a visible five-minute interval. Settings has Check for updates. A newer release shows an in-app notice with Save & update now and Later. Acceptance durably saves game/audio/studio work before worker activation and cache-busted reload; storage failures, temporary/recovery play or active imports block reload with recovery instructions. Other tabs do not reload automatically. These are in-app notifications, without OS notification permission or closed-app push. Existing1.4 windows must refresh/reopen once to load this first updater. Real desktop Chromium worker A→B and failed-save/retry/restore were tested; physical installed Pixel/Edge remains unverified.

Balanced records use /mahjong-scores-v2.html and a distinct scoring identity/type. The V1 service is retained unchanged; old pending entries keep their original payload/endpoint. Native V2 grammar/schema additionally verify official original pair counts, point arithmetic and stars/counters. Source policy remains tools/leaderboard-policy.mjs. Ordinary releases preserve both score documents. Manifest/worker are separately conditional mutable deployment controls after root promotion; all previous immutable graphs remain. Campaign output legally omits optional li closing tags and safe attribute quotes, with full parsed content equality checked; authored HTML is unchanged. Evidence and scoring review: audit/scoring/.

## Simple leaderboard (1.6.0)

The leaderboard opens on the current garden with its top ten and three columns: Rank, Name and Points. Your latest acknowledged result also appears if it falls outside the ten. Equal points share a rank. More contains other gardens, earlier History, manual refresh and scoring help. Name entry appears after an official level clear; it remembers your last submitted name. Saving shows the sheet and keeps an unsent result locally for Retry. You can continue to the next garden while a submission finishes. Existing shared scores, scoring, progress and update behavior remain compatible. Plan, handbook 2.13.0 snapshot and separate coverage/evidence review: `audit/simplify/`.

Automatic scores (1.6.1): once a name is recorded, official clears save publicly under it without another submit tap. The clear screen stays open; saving does not open the leaderboard. Unsent scores from several levels are retained in a bounded local queue and sent in order. Retry or a subsequent online event resumes after a network failure; acknowledged deals are not resubmitted. Local ledger 2 migrates the earlier name/pending/accepted data without changing legacy payloads. Game saves, scoring and the two shared score services are unchanged. First name entry remains explicit; custom studio clears stay private. The current completed checkpoint can save when restored; earlier best-star history cannot be backfilled as scores. Plan/evidence: `audit/autosave/`.

Home parallax (1.6.2): the existing mountains, pavilion and foreground move at three gentle depths in response to the pointer or a primary background touch. The title/menu stay fixed. Motion eases to its target and stops scheduling frames when settled; play, open menus, hidden pages and app/OS reduced motion reset it. Touches on controls and secondary fingers do not start it, and scrolling/pinch are not intercepted. No motion-sensor permission or new images. Plan/evidence: `audit/parallax/`.

Combined totals (1.7.0): each board score also shows that name's combined total. Overall compares the sum of each name's best current score on every board, plus its contributing board count. Replaying a board cannot inflate the total. Names group case-insensitively; they are public aliases, not authenticated accounts. Equal totals share rank. Both views show ten plus the latest acknowledged result/name when outside ten. Earlier stars/time History stays separate. The board view still opens on the current garden, with three columns and other filters/help under More. No score-record rewrite or save migration. Plan/evidence: `audit/totals/`.

Version 1.7.1 keeps the leaderboard's descriptive table caption available to screen readers without displaying an extra paragraph above the rows.


Leaderboard responsiveness (1.7.2): Rank stays on one line on narrow screens. A complete current or History dataset is reused in memory for 30 seconds, including Board / Overall / level changes and reopening. Expired rows stay visible during background revalidation; failed refreshes label older scores and offer Retry. More → Refresh always requests current scores. Opening starts the read independently of the local name/outbox ledger; confirmed submissions update the same dataset after durable acknowledgement. Optional pointer/focus intent warms the lazy leaderboard. First uncached load still needs network. Plan/evidence: `audit/leaderboard-speed/`.


Time-adjusted points (1.8.0): the completion dialog removes Stay here a moment and shows base points + time bonus. Faster active play adds up to10% of the assistance-adjusted base, scaled by original pair count. Final points = base + floor(base × pairs ÷ (10 × pairs + active seconds)). A clean12-pair clear earns10666 at60s,10500 at120s,10333 at240s. No deadline; menus/home/hidden pages pause the timer. Stars and assistance costs stay the same, Undo never refunds elapsed time, and seconds quantize identically for completion/submission. All current board ranks and best-board combined totals use this projection (`mg-time-points-1`), including existing recorded times. Raw balanced records, result IDs, queued payloads, services and saves stay compatible; no reset or server rewrite. Earlier stars/time History stays separate. Equal final points share rank. Plan and evidence: `audit/timed-score/`.

## Template adaptation

Reuses the full MIT Mahjong Garden source/history. Original audit entries describe the upstream release, not this template candidate. UI chrome uses Pagelove design-system tokens in brand.css; game rules/content retained. Run bun install, bun run check, then bun run prepare. Only generated site/ contents are installable. Set PAGELOVE_SITE_ORIGIN to the new HTTPS public origin before preparing; otherwise canonical metadata uses example.invalid. Sharing uses current browser origin. Original-host network publication is disabled; injected test transports remain available. No writes to the upstream game host are authorized. Same-origin shared boards require separately verified data policies; local progress remains independent.

Template installs can use a subdirectory: update checks/service-worker scope, manifest launch and challenge links stay inside the current app directory. An explicit PWA scope must equal that directory. Shared score services still require separately accepted same-site policies.

## Live fictional review

[Open this app preview](https://camel-boom-0460.onpagelove.com/template-review-20261105/mahjong-template/index.html) · [All app previews](https://camel-boom-0460.onpagelove.com/).

The disposable review copy contains only fictional data and is publicly accessible. Source files were staged create-only, then verified through both owner WebDAV and public reads. Browser tasks loaded the deployed app. A390×844 browser viewport was checked; this is emulation, not physical-phone acceptance.

Live first-level hint-to-win journey passed. Subdirectory-scoped update handling and relative launch/share links are included. Shared score services remain unaccepted.

Pagelove native authentication has not been shown to fail. A401 on an application route with no matching write grant is not evidence that a separate identity system is required. Owner WebDAV authoring is already authenticated; browser actor/session integration and exact per-app read/write rules remain to be established before enabling protected functions. Public reading and local game play need no account by themselves.

## Slide 4 build and deploy

Use the repository URL, site hostname and private API token supplied in the generated prompt. After adapting and checking the app, run `node scripts/deploy.mjs --prepare`, then `node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com`. The token is entered privately; existing records are retained. See [deployment instructions](docs/deployment.md) for verify/update commands, isolated paths and exact guarantees. No console-session handoff is required for trusted authoring deployment. Published browser code never contains the owner token.

## Document-first development review

Read [the edition2.4 project record](DOCUMENT-FIRST-REVIEW.md) for source authority, operation/recovery contracts, justified runtime exceptions and current acceptance limits. Plans and verification are recorded in audit/CHANGELOG.md. Local tests do not establish live privacy, authorization or physical-device acceptance.

The collection finder searches actual names/descriptions and filters completed or unplayed content; Racing also filters available circuits without unlocking locked events. Clear filters restores the collection. View state never changes game records.

# Document-first review — Mahjong

Guide: Pagelove Document-first development edition2.4, revised2026-11-04; supplied source SHA256 `322d0c1c1c016787edeb67702c62c69610f26916933d0f34ec3dd7b2468b26dc`. Actor: Codex. Review source: `5b0f2d5d709a98ce7c3d3b58b9a791f92087b84d`. Maintainer: repository maintainers. Profiles: A5/A6.

## Model, authority and lifecycle

content/levels.html is authoritative level/layout content. tools/build.mjs derives immutable dist/site gameplay packages; core/garden models parse authored content. Personal photos are media; run timers/tile positions and compact checkpoint encoding are specialized A6 state, not competing editable level definitions.

## Operation, state and recovery contract

Stable level IDs and source digests identify definitions; game progress, studio drafts, undo and checkpoints use existing versioned local storage contracts. Shared scores are separately configured and remain unaccepted for a new target until checked. Owner CLI install preserves existing records and unrelated paths.

See GAME-PLAN.md, REVIEW.md, tools/contracts.mjs and scoring/storage tests for bounds, bytes and version policies. Imported unsupported/hostile content is rejected and existing progress retained. Exact live shared board policy, real phone and assistive acceptance remain separate.

## Enforcement and effects

Only fictional/public preview and local gameplay acceptance are claimed. No anti-cheat, production private-data or provider-wide authorization guarantee from passing local game tests.

## W1–W8 / R01–R12 acceptance

- W1–W3 / R01–R04: selected profiles, HTML preference, stable identities, owned aggregates and the representation exception above are the governing source contract. Derived caches/runtime arrays cannot become independent editable authorities.
- W4 / R05–R07: inspect exact canonical address/selector, actor, source revision and actual enforcement before enabling a newly relied-on mutation. Local fixtures and declaration review do not establish target-host privacy or validation.
- W5–W6 / R08–R10: distinguish working draft, frozen pending command, accepted state and unknown outcome. Preserve original data on rejected/future imports. No automatic external-effect replay. Offline collaboration/subscription features are not implied by browser storage; add tested scope/disposal/reconnect contracts before offering them.
- W7–W8 / R09–R12: audit/CHANGELOG.md records current commands, revisions and results. Existing REVIEW evidence remains historical. Re-run the appropriate source/shape/round-trip/concurrency/negative checks, then actual affected browser tasks. Never label pending live, maximum-device, assistive, restore or security checks as passed.

## Release and maintenance gates

Preserve user records, mutable source paths and incompatible backups during code updates. Do not replace a live document containing user records with a seed. Exclude credentials/private payloads from source, logs, public examples and previews. Pin coupled runtime/definition versions and retain rollback assets. Before real private or consequential use, verify supported read/write paths with valid and known-invalid/unauthorized requests on the actual host, exercise restoration in isolation, and record device/performance/accessibility limits. No new service or identity provider is authorized by this record. Re-review when format, source route, write adapter, host configuration, rules or runtime changes.

# Prompt-driven build and deployment

Slide 4 supplies the selected repository URL, public site hostname and private API token to the user's coding AI. The AI reads this repository's instructions, adapts the actual app, runs its checks, prepares site/ and deploys that directory using trusted owner WebDAV authoring. This flow does not require a console-to-app browser session handoff. No outside identity provider is used.

## Commands

Use Node22 or newer. Install pinned development dependencies with npm install or bun install --ignore-scripts. Run the repository's check and test commands, plus node --test tests/deployment.test.mjs. For Mahjong, run node tools/prepare-template.mjs after changing game source; other apps already author their runtime under site/.

1. node scripts/deploy.mjs --prepare — validate the prepared installation closure and scan for credentials. This does not create a site or upload anything.
2. node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com — paste the account API token at the private terminal prompt. Terminal echo is disabled. An automation may instead receive PAGELOVE_API_TOKEN through its private credential mechanism; never put a real token in shell command text, a prompt transcript committed to Git, browser code, URLs or logs.
3. node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com --verify — read-only owner/public verification of the prepared release.

Use --path /isolated-directory/ for a separate install on an existing authorized test site. Root / is the default for the user's own selected site. The tool only accepts an exact native onpagelove.com hostname and its corresponding dav- hostname; custom domains need an explicitly reviewed adaptation. Network redirects are refused. Site creation and connection provisioning are handled by Pagelove, before this command.

## Preservation and updates

The tool inventories the destination and preflights the complete payload before writing. Fresh files and records use If-None-Match: *. Existing records/, data/, submissions/ and scores/ resources are retained, including owner edits; unrelated files are never deleted. Existing different code is refused unless you inspect it and deliberately pass --update. Code updates require a strong ETag and If-Match; stale412 and network ambiguity stop without automatic retry. Assets are uploaded before index.html. Publication across several files is not one atomic transaction; retain old immutable assets when designing release changes.

Every installed file is read back through owner authoring. HTML is compared by parsed structure to accommodate platform serialization; other payloads are byte-compared. The public entry is also checked, ignoring only the known platform branding footer. Existing mutable records are verified against the destination baseline, not reset to template seeds. The sanitized receipt is stored in ignored .local/deployment-receipt.json. It contains paths/hashes/results, never the token. It is verification evidence, not a backup. Back up real records privately before a migration and verify restoration separately.

## What this establishes

A successful run establishes build-payload installation and readback on the selected site. Browser review still checks actual user journeys and network assets. The supplied token stays in the coding AI's private authoring process; the published app never receives it.

Browser-based private record editing, protected drafts and booking administration remain separate supported-authentication/authorization integrations. Do not add a fake signed-in flag or embed the owner token to enable them. Use fictional review data until the target's protected read/write paths are accepted. Games retain device-local progress as documented. A deployment succeeds independently of these optional runtime integrations; it does not claim they passed.

Official references: https://docs.pagelove.com/ and https://docs.pagelove.com/reference/reading-and-writing/ . Follow docs/architecture.md (where present), REVIEW.md and the document-first guide for the actual app's authority and limitations.

# Racing · Scrap League

A fuller Racing template based on [Scrap League](https://github.com/wesley83/scrap-league). Twelve authored circuits, four cups,81 modular car builds, six-car races, Time Trial, Daily Spec, local progress/ghosts and the integrated Track Workshop. See [actual implementation boundaries](IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md), [source provenance](UPSTREAM.md) and [document-first architecture](docs/architecture.md).

Install with bun install --ignore-scripts (or npm install), run node tools/build.mjs and node --test tests/*.test.mjs, then node tools/serve.mjs. The normal build validates content/ and produces site/; never rerun destructive author-content utilities as part of a build.

Slide4 combines this repo, the user's site hostname and private API token. Run node scripts/deploy.mjs --prepare, then node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com. Enter the token privately. Use --path /isolated-directory/ for a separate test install and --verify for read-only verification. Existing differing entry code requires deliberate --update. See docs/deployment.md for exact semantics. No separate account/auth service is needed for owner deployment.

Gameplay, garage and Workshop drafts save on this browser. Shared boards and remote Workshop publishing are disconnected. No owner token is embedded. Old Roundabout progress is left untouched; it is not imported as a Scrap League result.

## Document-first development review

2. node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com — paste the account API token at the private terminal prompt. Terminal echo is disabled. An automation may instead receive PAGELOVE_API_TOKEN through its private credential mechanism; never put a real token in shell command text, a prompt transcript committed to Git, browser code, URLs or logs.
3. node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com --verify — read-only owner/public verification of the prepared release.

Use --path /isolated-directory/ for a separate install on an existing authorized test site. Root / is the default for the user's own selected site. The tool only accepts an exact native onpagelove.com hostname and its corresponding dav- hostname; custom domains need an explicitly reviewed adaptation. Network redirects are refused. Site creation and connection provisioning are handled by Pagelove, before this command.

## Preservation and updates

The tool inventories the destination and preflights the complete payload before writing. Fresh files and records use If-None-Match: *. Existing records/, data/, submissions/ and scores/ resources are retained, including owner edits; unrelated files are never deleted. Existing different code is refused unless you inspect it and deliberately pass --update. Code updates require a strong ETag and If-Match; stale412 and network ambiguity stop without automatic retry. Assets are uploaded before index.html. Publication across several files is not one atomic transaction; retain old immutable assets when designing release changes.

Every installed file is read back through owner authoring. HTML is compared by parsed structure to accommodate platform serialization; other payloads are byte-compared. The public entry is also checked, ignoring only the known platform branding footer. Existing mutable records are verified against the destination baseline, not reset to template seeds. The sanitized receipt is stored in ignored .local/deployment-receipt.json. It contains paths/hashes/results, never the token. It is verification evidence, not a backup. Back up real records privately before a migration and verify restoration separately.

## What this establishes

A successful run establishes build-payload installation and readback on the selected site. Browser review still checks actual user journeys and network assets. The supplied token stays in the coding AI's private authoring process; the published app never receives it.

# Prompt-driven build and deployment

Slide 4 supplies the selected repository URL, public site hostname and private API token to the user's coding AI. The AI reads this repository's instructions, adapts the actual app, runs its checks, prepares site/ and deploys that directory using trusted owner WebDAV authoring. This flow does not require a console-to-app browser session handoff. No outside identity provider is used.

## Commands

Use Node22 or newer. Install pinned development dependencies with npm install or bun install --ignore-scripts. Run the repository's check and test commands, plus node --test tests/deployment.test.mjs. For Mahjong, run node tools/prepare-template.mjs after changing game source; other apps already author their runtime under site/.

1. node scripts/deploy.mjs --prepare — validate the prepared installation closure and scan for credentials. This does not create a site or upload anything.
2. node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com — paste the account API token at the private terminal prompt. Terminal echo is disabled. An automation may instead receive PAGELOVE_API_TOKEN through its private credential mechanism; never put a real token in shell command text, a prompt transcript committed to Git, browser code, URLs or logs.
3. node scripts/deploy.mjs --host YOUR-SITE.onpagelove.com --verify — read-only owner/public verification of the prepared release.

Use --path /isolated-directory/ for a separate install on an existing authorized test site. Root / is the default for the user's own selected site. The tool only accepts an exact native onpagelove.com hostname and its corresponding dav- hostname; custom domains need an explicitly reviewed adaptation. Network redirects are refused. Site creation and connection provisioning are handled by Pagelove, before this command.

## Preservation and updates

The tool inventories the destination and preflights the complete payload before writing. Fresh files and records use If-None-Match: *. Existing records/, data/, submissions/ and scores/ resources are retained, including owner edits; unrelated files are never deleted. Existing different code is refused unless you inspect it and deliberately pass --update. Code updates require a strong ETag and If-Match; stale412 and network ambiguity stop without automatic retry. Assets are uploaded before index.html. Publication across several files is not one atomic transaction; retain old immutable assets when designing release changes.

Every installed file is read back through owner authoring. HTML is compared by parsed structure to accommodate platform serialization; other payloads are byte-compared. The public entry is also checked, ignoring only the known platform branding footer. Existing mutable records are verified against the destination baseline, not reset to template seeds. The sanitized receipt is stored in ignored .local/deployment-receipt.json. It contains paths/hashes/results, never the token. It is verification evidence, not a backup. Back up real records privately before a migration and verify restoration separately.

## What this establishes

A successful run establishes build-payload installation and readback on the selected site. Browser review still checks actual user journeys and network assets. The supplied token stays in the coding AI's private authoring process; the published app never receives it.

[Hosted sample](https://some-derby-0862.onpagelove.com/crm-demo/) · [Design notes](DESIGN.md)

Keep a contact roster, follow-up cadence, and conversation history. Search and due filters are local views. Conversations are saved before updating follow-up dates; partial-save recovery retries only the due-date update. Data lives in `#people` and `#log`. The private variant under `tests/fixtures/` is a sanitized regression fixture, not a deployed page.

## Run locally

Use Python 3.10 or later:

```sh
python -m venv .venv
# Activate the environment for your shell, then:
python -m pip install -r requirements-preview.txt
python preview.py
```

Open [the local app](http://127.0.0.1:8787/crm-demo/). The server binds to loopback only. Use `--port 8788` if the default port is occupied. Changes are saved in `.preview-state/`, which Git ignores. Use `--state-dir .preview-state/fresh` for a separate sample session.

## Install from the Pagelove console

Kin is in the console's template catalogue. Open an empty host in the console, choose Kin and select Add template. The console copies the contents of `site/` to the host root.

`pagelove.html` describes the template to the console. It is never installed.

`site/` is the complete deployment directory. Upload **its contents** to the root of a new Pagelove host, preserving `crm-demo/` and `assets/`. The root page redirects to `/crm-demo/`.

4. Create missing collections with `MKCOL`, upload assets first, then the app files with WebDAV `PUT`. Upload the root landing page last.
5. Read back the uploaded files and check the application through the separate public hostname.

Use a fresh host or back up existing documents first. The HTML contains both the app and seed records: replacing it can overwrite live data. bun install --frozen-lockfile

# Kin: personal CRM

Direction: a warm, practical contact notebook. The September 6 refinement puts the last conversation, next follow-up and contact schedule at the center of the interface. Portraits are small identifiers; the app uses direct labels and readable text.

## Color and type

Warm white `#FBF9F5` supports reading, brown `#382D28` carries primary text, and terracotta `#8F4832` marks actions and selection. Borders and supporting text stay in the same warm family. Dark mode changes these semantic variables consistently.

Manrope is the working typeface, with 14–16px body text and supporting details at least 12px. Source Serif 4 is limited to the Kin wordmark and page title. Names and notes wrap instead of truncating.

## Layout

Desktop uses a contact roster alongside the selected person's details and a conversation/history workspace. The selected-person summary contains a small avatar, actual last conversation date, actual next follow-up date, plain cadence text, and the last saved note. Tablet and mobile stack the form and history where space requires it. Mobile uses a single contact list and 16px form controls.

The large arched portrait, decorative progress rings, poetic empty states and uppercase labels are removed. Cadence is stated as “Every 30 days” rather than implying an activity or relationship progress score.

## Data and interaction boundaries

- Only the original Ana and Ben sample IDs use small square crops from the fictional portrait atlas. New contacts use initials. The footer explains the sample imagery, and named avatar alternatives identify it as fictional.
- Dates, contact schedules and notes come from the existing records. No relationship facts or shared interests are invented.
- Search, due filters, selection, forms, draft ownership guards, error visibility and partial-write recovery remain unchanged.
- The ordinary Refresh control stays disabled during a pending write. The explicit recovery button retries the required step without duplicating an interaction.

The package serves `site/assets/Manrope-Variable.woff2` and `site/assets/crm-portraits.webp` at their `/assets/` URLs. A deployment must preserve those paths. Ship the CRM-local Source Serif font, favicon, stylesheets and JavaScript as well. No runtime CDN is used.

# Fieldwork visual system

## Direction

A straightforward invoice tracker for independent work. Client names, amounts, due dates, and the next available action take priority. The ink navigation and cobalt actions identify the application; the document preview looks like the invoice a client would receive.

The balance summary is compact and uses the same visual language as the register. Avoid oversized metric tiles, slogans, decorative punctuation, uppercase eyebrows, ornamental marks, or panels that do not group a specific task.

## Colors

| Token | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Ink | `#172237` | Primary text |
| Rail | `#121B2E` | Desktop navigation |
| Cobalt | `#254BE7` | Primary actions, outstanding amount, selection, invoice rule |
| Canvas | `#F4F6FA` | Application background |
| Paper | `#FFFFFF` | Ledger and printable invoice |
| Line | `#E0E5EF` | Rows and section dividers |
| Muted | `#5E6B80` | Supporting information |

Green, coral, and gray identify paid, overdue, and inactive statuses. Always pair the color with a written status. The summary contains actual invoice totals; no decorative charts or implied trends are added.

## Typography

Space Grotesk is used for the app name, headings, and numbers. Manrope carries the controls and working copy. Source Serif appears in the invoice sender's name. Fonts are self-hosted at `/assets/SpaceGrotesk-Variable.woff2`, `/assets/Manrope-Variable.woff2`, and `/assets/SourceSerif4-Variable.woff`.

Normal application text is 14–16px. Supporting metadata, status labels, dates, and footer text use 12px where practical. Client names and financial amounts are easier to scan than invoice identifiers. The document preview uses 13–14px body text on wider screens and 12–13px on phones; print has its own larger page layout. Mobile editing inputs use 16px.

## Layout and behavior

- Desktop: an ink navigation rail, compact page heading and balance summary, a client register, and the selected invoice beside it.
- Tablet: a horizontal masthead preserves readable labels instead of reducing the rail to icons. The register and detail view stack below 850px.
- Phone: a compact 2×2 balance summary, clear client and amount rows, and separate invoice-number and due-date lines. The next action appears before the paper invoice.
- Actions: mark sent, record payment, and void controls are placed directly below the selected invoice's heading. Confirmation stays with the action. Status explanations use direct, factual copy.
- Drafts: field groups are named Invoice details, From, Bill to, Line items, and Notes. The composer retains its visible refresh control after an unconfirmed save. Reopening Create invoice returns to the existing draft. Successful draft saves move keyboard focus to the refreshed invoice after controls unlock; cancel returns to the opening control.
- Print: only the selected invoice remains. Root backgrounds are white; the application, action controls, and summary are hidden. The fictional-sample notice remains on the invoice.
- Without JavaScript: `no-script.css` hides inert loading controls and shows a plain explanation with readable copy. Real demo navigation remains available.
- Reduced motion: animations and transitions are disabled when requested.

## Preservation and QA

Keep the raw record collection, schema/auth/transition metadata, cents arithmetic, ETags, and uncertain-save recovery intact when changing presentation. All ten invoice regression tests passed after the September 6 refinement. Browser review must include desktop, phone, composer, error recovery, no-JavaScript, and print views. Local preview evidence does not establish live Pagelove authorization or constraint enforcement.

Public fictional client details only. Actual private-read/write/schema/uniqueness enforcement is not established by mocked HTTP tests or authoring upload.

Preserve user records, mutable source paths and incompatible backups during code updates. Do not replace a live document containing user records with a seed. Before real private or consequential use, verify supported read/write paths with valid and known-invalid/unauthorized requests on the actual host, exercise restoration in isolation, and record device/performance/accessibility limits. No new service or identity provider is authorized by this record. Re-review when format, source route, write adapter, host configuration, rules or runtime changes.

# Prism Breaker

![Prism Breaker](public/assets/og-prism-breaker.jpg)

A colorful brick-breaker game built with Three.js on [Pagelove](https://pagelove.com). Explore sixteen 3D worlds, catch glowing power-ups, watch cinematic transitions, and chase shared high scores.

**[Play the game](https://sane-guild-8399.onpagelove.com/)** · **[Public source](https://github.com/pagelove/prism-breaker)**

The browser runs the gameplay and creates the music and scorecards. Native Pagelove routes and composed templates power the world editor; editable worlds are stored as HTML microdata. Pagelove hosts the complete site and stores and validates shared scores through HTML resources. No separate application server, external runtime API, or CDN is required.

## Game features

- **Adventure:** sixteen themed worlds and twenty formations. Prism Citadel is a three-formation midpoint; Dawn Nexus is the three-formation finale. Existing checkpoints can continue into the second half.
- **Daily Challenge:** one world selected from a UTC-date seed, with shared launch and power-up random sequences. Its active leaderboard rolls over at 00:00 UTC.
- **Practice:** play individual worlds, including shared edited HTML layouts and custom brick recipes. Practice scores stay out of the shared boards and personal best.
- **World workshop:** native `/editor/<worldname>` routes, inspectable HTML microdata, visual brick editing, undo/redo, local drafts, import/export, custom types and a Three.js play preview. Owner publishing uses ETags and preserves concurrent edits. See [WORLD-EDITOR.md](WORLD-EDITOR.md).
- **Brick mechanics:** armored, moving, explosive and switch bricks, gates, moving barriers and paired portals. Worlds 3–6 have a modest difficulty increase.
- **Brick labels:** armored bricks show their remaining hit count in distinct colors: cyan 3, gold 2, coral 1. Explosives use a filled star and switches an outlined diamond. How to play explains each type with matching visual examples.
- **Crystal artwork:** the stacked vector wordmark follows the OG lettering. Bricks have beveled gemstone geometry, translucent colored faces and local studio reflections. Armored bricks accumulate branching cracks after each surviving hit.
- **OG-style paddle:** a dark inset face, polished beveled frame and glowing cyan/pink end brackets. Wide Paddle extends the body while preserving the cap proportions; Sticky adds an amber rail and Laser adds a red rail and visible emitters.
- **Classic mode:** an optional saved setting restores the original opaque rectangular bricks and pale paddle with its colored stripe. Colored hit counts remain available. Switching styles preserves the current run and its power-ups; the brick legend follows the selected appearance.
- **Eight power-ups:** wide paddle, multiball, sticky paddle, laser, piercing ball, slow motion, safety shield and extra life. Sticky catches hold at the impact position; a shrinking wide paddle releases catches beyond its new edge.
- **Full paddle contacts:** swept collisions include the lower solid body and raised endcaps. The [paddle follow-up](PADDLE-COLLISION-FOLLOWUP.md) documents two reproduced misses, independent geometry checks and the local before/after replay.
- **Fresh-ball variation:** new balls launch 8–18° left or right of vertical. Checkpoints preserve sequence progress, while sticky catches retain their rebound direction.
- **Cinematics:** sixteen distinct procedural sets with establishing, activation and reveal shots, local reflections, layered atmosphere, bloom, and readable captions. Daily completion, the daily crown and Adventure champion have separate sequences. Reduced-motion compositions and lower-cost rendering remain available.
- **Procedural audio:** sixteen original synthesized level soundtracks, two victory arrangements and sound effects, with separate volume controls and mute.
- **Score display and shared records:** the current player's score is centered in larger, bold type, with readable thousands separators. The board leader's name and score appear on the left; lives and pause stay on the right. Adventure and Daily Challenge have separate top-25 rankings; the daily board displays minutes since submission. Adventure rows have a full green outline through 48 hours, yellow over 48–96 hours, and red over 96 hours. These age indicators update while the board stays open; both boards explain the five-day expiry.
- **Sharing:** leaderboard invitations and personal scorecards, native sharing where supported, complete-message copying, PNG downloads and QR codes. Android invitations combine message and link into one text body; daily dates use readable UTC labels.
- **Presentation and access:** responsive keyboard/mouse/touch controls, fullscreen launch for installed apps where supported, automatic phone fullscreen from start/resume taps, pause-menu settings, reduced motion/effects, light/dark/system interface themes and readable cinematic captions. Phone gameplay fills the available viewport when native fullscreen is unavailable, with space for notches and gesture areas.
- **Progress:** campaign checkpoints, personal best, preferences and the last entered nickname persist in browser storage.
- **Offline play and installation:** install the game or keep playing in a browser tab after its complete download. All worlds, music, cinematics and scorecards work offline; saved scores queue for reconnection.
- **Safe updates:** complete releases download before becoming available. Players apply updates from the start screen; open games retain their existing assets.
- **Performance:** active play targets 60 FPS independently of the 120 Hz physics step. Crystal bodies, edges, count/crack artwork, scenery and bounded particles use shared GPU batches; resolution adapts to sustained load. Low effects uses simpler crystal lighting, gameplay uses glow sprites, and cinematic bloom stays in the cut scenes. Shaders/textures prepare before play, hidden pages stop rendering, and muted music stops scheduling new voices. See [rendering performance](RENDER-PERFORMANCE.md) for limits and reproducible measurements.
- **Social artwork:** SVG/ICO/PNG favicons, touch icons, and landscape/square Open Graph and Twitter card images.

## Mastery and engagement

The new engagement implementation adds four independent medals per world, personal world records and next-goal feedback; paired power choices and three strategies; an earned aimed Precision catch for slow board endings; Citadel, Thunder Spire and Nexus core encounters; reachable score comparisons and shared official Practice challenges; authored barrier/music recovery periods; and cosmetic finishes, trails, restored artwork and soundtrack rewards. The proposed short-session mode is excluded.

Goals, encounters, pacing and unlocks are authored in [engagement.html](public/engagement.html) and validated into an offline runtime projection. Old checkpoints retain their original rules; changed gameplay gets its own score revision. Progress can be exported/imported, while optional bounded play notes remain local. See [ENGAGEMENT.md](ENGAGEMENT.md) for controls, tuning, privacy, compatibility and validation limits. This source implementation has not yet been deployed or given new release acceptance evidence.

## Document-first architecture

World metadata and formations are authoritative HTML documents. The catalog provides permanent IDs, campaign order and legacy mappings; the build produces the complete offline runtime snapshot without depending on its previous output. Practice reads the same model, including edited instructions, narratives, colors and scene/music presets.

- [Architecture and all 23 standards](DOCUMENT-FIRST-ARCHITECTURE.md): ownership, events, versioning, recovery, offline state and justified runtime exceptions.
- [Reusable development rule](DOCUMENT-FIRST-DEVELOPMENT.md): the governing project philosophy.
- [Complete game-development handbook](GAME-DEVELOPMENT-BEST-PRACTICES.md): reusable architecture, gameplay, balance, leaderboards, artwork, accessibility, PWA, review and release practices, including the complete parent document-first rule and lessons from the audit history.
- [Implementation audit](audit/2026-10-14-document-first-implementation.md): exact verification and deployment status. Local completion does not establish live enforcement.

Checkpoint v2 stores stable world identity, definition and ruleset revisions, and a complete definition including portals. Compatible legacy saves migrate; incompatible saves remain recoverable. Scores carry an optional ruleset fingerprint, and rankings compare compatible rulesets. Existing unversioned scores use a frozen legacy mapping.

The editor validates world writes with the shared schema, uses owner-only DAV access, sends an ETag condition and confirms the saved document by reading it back. **Support confirmed that WebDAV intentionally bypasses all schema validation and triggers; it is only an authoring mechanism.** This is expected behavior, not a platform enforcement bug. The generated trigger candidate stays inactive outside deployed assets in policy-candidates/ and cannot enforce DAV authoring. Wesley chose to retain owner DAV publishing only; no application-write grant is added. No anonymous world-write grant was added. See the [resolved report](DAV-TRIGGER-BUG-REPORT.md) and [architecture boundary](DOCUMENT-FIRST-ARCHITECTURE.md#persistence-boundary).

| 7. Cosmic Reef | Everything connects | Tidal Orbit |

## Technology

| Custom JavaScript physics | Ball/paddle/brick collisions in the arena’s 2D plane, power-ups and scoring; a fixed 120 Hz simulation driven by `requestAnimationFrame` |
| Web Audio API | Oscillators, envelopes, synthesized percussion, reverb and scheduled music; no downloaded music files |
| Canvas 2D and Blob/File APIs | Runtime scorecard images, glow/symbol textures and local PNG downloads |

Bun runs the development tools and tests; a separate Node.js installation is not required. Existing `node:*` imports, including `node:test`, use [Bun’s Node.js compatibility layer](https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/nodejs-compat). The deployed game runs in the browser and Pagelove.

All browser runtime code, fonts, icons, images, QR encoding and postprocessing files are included in `public/`. Installing development dependencies is optional when playing or serving the committed site.

## Pagelove features used

Pagelove supplies the shared data store, request rules, server composition and owner authoring endpoint. The following capabilities are implemented in this repository; the source links show where each one is configured or called.

| Pagelove capability | How Prism Breaker uses it | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Selector-based HTTP reads | `GET /scores.html` with `Range: selector=#scores` returns the shared leaderboard fragment. The client reads its microdata to build the Adventure and Daily rankings. | [Score client](public/app.js) |

| HTML microdata as structured data | Score records carry typed properties such as player, score, mode, day and expiry. World documents contain nested formations, rows, bricks, custom types, barriers and portals. HTML microdata is a web standard that Pagelove can store, compose and process. | [Score schema generator](tools/build-data.mjs), [example world](public/worlds/prism-garden/definition.html), [world parser](public/world-format.js) |
| Parameterized routes | The stored route `/editor/:worldname` serves addresses such as `/editor/prism-garden`. Pagelove exposes the captured slug through `Context.request.params.worldname`. | [Editor route](public/editor-route.html), [route builder](tools/build-editor.mjs) |
| Reusable templates and native fragment composition | `p:include` selects `#editor-shell` from a shared template and `#world` from the chosen world document. The world catalog composes all sixteen world fragments. | [Editor shell](public/editor-template.html), [world catalog](public/worlds.html) |
| Schema methods and server-side JavaScript | The `urn:PrismBreaker:EditorTemplate` schema defines a `world` method. Its JavaScript implementation checks the route slug against the sixteen supported worlds and returns that world's native include. | [Editor route](public/editor-route.html) |
| Declarative authorization | Anonymous visitors may append scores only within `#scores`. Publishing site files and shared world edits requires the owner's credential; that credential is never embedded in the released assets. | [Authorization rules](public/scores.html), [editor publisher](public/editor.js) |
| Shape constraints | The score container accepts only the configured list, run and property markup. This constrains the HTML structure accepted by the shared resource. | [Shape rules](tools/build-data.mjs) |
| Typed schemas, cardinality and uniqueness | Required properties have declared types and counts. A unique `runKey` supports retrying an interrupted submission without creating a second accepted run. `submittedAt` remains optional for compatibility with older records. | [Score schema](tools/build-data.mjs), [submission queue](public/offline.js) |
| Request triggers with Sessel | A POST trigger checks the exact one-run payload grammar, nickname format, mode and numeric bounds; rejected submissions receive HTTP 422. | [Sessel trigger](tools/build-data.mjs) |
| Computed server defaults | Pagelove supplies `expiresAt` as server time plus five days. The POST grammar does not accept a client-chosen expiry, so changing the submitted payload cannot extend that deadline. | [Expiry property](tools/retention-rules.mjs) |
| Guarded selector DELETE | A DELETE trigger permits only the exact expired-row selector and rejects cutoffs later than server time. The client can request cleanup without gaining permission to delete arbitrary scores. | [Retention rules](tools/retention-rules.mjs), [cleanup client](public/app.js) |

| World validation boundary | The shared schema validates editor/build/import data; owner DAV publishing uses ETags and readback. The 3D renderer, physics, music, CSS brick styling, DOM strike/damage events, PWA installation, offline cache and sharing run through ordinary browser APIs and bundled JavaScript. Pagelove stores and composes the HTML that those features consume. There is no external runtime API, database, CDN or scheduling service in this design.

### World editor flow

1. A visitor opens [the workshop](https://sane-guild-8399.onpagelove.com/editor/prism-garden). Pagelove resolves `/editor/:worldname`, executes its schema method and composes the shared shell with `/worlds/prism-garden/definition.html`'s `#world` fragment.
2. Browser code validates that HTML and exposes visual editing, local drafts, undo/redo and a Three.js preview. Bricks retain their microdata types, so CSS selectors such as `[itemtype~="urn:Brick:Moving"]` can style specializations and application code can handle their strike events.
3. An owner can publish through the editor using the existing host key. The editor checks the current document and ETag, writes with `If-Match`, and verifies the result. The key is cleared from the input and is not saved in drafts, exports or browser storage.
4. Practice loads the published world. Adventure and Daily Challenge use the official offline snapshot generated from the checked-in HTML definitions, so a live edit does not change an ongoing ranked challenge. Normal deployments exclude mutable world documents.

Opening the native editor requires a connection. The type builder combines supported behavior recipes; arbitrary new physics or rendering still requires trusted application code. See [WORLD-EDITOR.md](WORLD-EDITOR.md) for the data format, event API and publishing details.

### Leaderboard flow

1. The browser loads `public/index.html` and its same-origin modules/assets.
2. Official play uses a validated, revisioned offline snapshot of complete world definitions generated from the catalog and checked-in HTML worlds. Practice fetches the selected shared world document, or uses a cached published world, saved draft, or original release when the network is unavailable.
3. Gameplay, collisions, music and score calculation happen in the browser.
4. When a player chooses **Save score**, the client commits the run to its IndexedDB queue, then attempts to post one HTML record to the score selector. Pagelove applies the authorization, shape, schema and trigger rules.
5. A successful submission leaves a local receipt. Interrupted requests retry with the same unique run key; an already accepted run is recognized through a fresh leaderboard read.
6. The client reads the shared records, filters out expired entries and other modes/challenge days, and ranks the top 25. Native cleanup removes expired stored rows; the client provides a guarded fallback. It saves a snapshot for offline display.

Leaderboards refresh at run start, after submission, on focus/visibility changes, through the Refresh button, and periodically during visible play. Updates use HTTP requests; the game does not use a WebSocket or server-event subscription.

Five-day expiry removes an entry from eligible rankings as soon as its deadline passes. Physical deletion is request-driven: the native GET processor and guarded client fallback remove expired rows when the online board is accessed. There is no background timer that deletes stored rows while the site receives no traffic. Daily rollover is a separate browser rule that selects the new UTC challenge date; it does not reset the whole stored score document at midnight.

### Daily Challenge and score records

- A daily seed comes from the UTC date at run start. All players for that challenge get the same world and the same fresh-launch sequence. Power-up randomness uses a separate seeded generator.
- The client schedules a midnight rollover and checks the date when returning to the game. The host's HTTP `Date` header helps align its clock.
- **Rollover filters the active board to the new date.** Both Adventure and Daily entries have a maximum five-day ranking lifetime and are automatically removed from storage on online access after expiry.
- A run crossing midnight keeps its original challenge day. It can be saved under that day, but does not appear on the new day's active board.
- Offline submissions also retain that original day. The server-generated expiry deadline starts the five-day window on submission, so an offline run receives its full window when it first reaches the server.
- Daily share links open the current daily leaderboard. Invitation text and PNG cards capture the record/date shown when the share preview opens.
- Scores and elapsed play time are supplied by the client. Nicknames are public, accountless labels. Current board age is derived from the server expiry deadline; client timestamps cannot extend retention.
- Rules accept scores from **0 to 1,000,000**, worlds **1–16**, durations **1–99,999 seconds**, and nicknames of **2–16 ASCII letters, numbers, spaces, dashes or underscores**. Practice submissions are excluded.
- Ranking orders by score descending, world reached descending, then elapsed active time ascending. A tied top score can qualify for a record celebration.

These rules validate record structure and ranges. Scores are self-reported; there is no authoritative replay verification or account identity. The client currently reads the full score container and applies the top-25 limit locally. Pagination and additional anti-abuse measures would require further work as the board grows.

### Five-day retention

- The schema assigns expiresAt = server time + 432,000,000 ms once. The exact POST grammar excludes that field, so players cannot choose a later deadline. Later submissions do not refresh existing rows.
- Rankings, high-score qualification, HUD leaders and share previews exclude expired records. Cached offline standings use the same rule and the last learned server clock offset.
- A native GET processor sees expired rows in its response and queues an anonymous, same-host DELETE. The server permits only the exact expiry selector and rejects a cutoff later than server time. A client fallback requests the same guarded cleanup.
- There is no idle timer: expired rows become ineligible immediately, but physical deletion happens on the next online read/open, or periodic refresh while a client remains open. A completely unvisited host can retain expired storage until that access.
- Migration preserves dated runs' original deadlines. Twelve legacy rows had no timestamp; those receive a five-day window from this migration instead of being discarded without evidence of their age. Future records always have a server deadline.
- Existing Daily Challenge selection is preserved through October 14, 2026 UTC; the sixteen-world daily pool begins October 15 at 00:00 UTC so a challenge does not change during its day.

## Install and play offline

Open the game while connected and wait for **Ready to play offline**. The service worker downloads all sixteen worlds' code and artwork, fonts, music code, cinematics and sharing assets: currently **73 cached files, approximately 2.43 MB** before browser storage overhead. Installation is optional; a prepared browser tab also works offline. The authoring catalog remains online; its generated runtime representation is included in the offline world bundle.

- **Android:** use **Install game** or the browser's **Install app / Add to Home screen** command.
- **iPhone and iPad:** use the browser's Share menu, then **Add to Home Screen**.
- **Desktop:** use the browser's install control when available. The game shows installation instructions if a native prompt is unavailable.

| Feature | Offline behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Adventure, Practice and Daily Challenge | Fully playable; the daily world uses the UTC date and the most recently learned server clock offset |
| Music, power-ups, cinematics and scorecards | Available from the downloaded game; no separate media service |
| Campaign progress and preferences | Saved as usual; checkpoint validation rejects damaged or incompatible records |
| Leaderboards | Show the last downloaded standings and refresh time; a fresh server read is required to confirm a top-score celebration |
| Save score | Durably queues the run; sends when the game is open and a connection returns |
| Rejected submissions | Remain visible with Retry and Remove controls; temporary failures retry with backoff |

An update downloads into a separate release cache and becomes available only after the full asset set passes its checks. **Update game** becomes usable on the start screen. It reloads into the new release while retaining progress, preferences and pending scores. Open tabs keep their release's assets, including modules loaded later. Pagelove selector responses and score writes bypass the static asset cache.

An activation failure offers another **Update game** attempt. If play starts while activation is finishing, the requested reload waits until the start screen. The reproducible browser lab (`bun tools/update-lab.mjs`, loopback port 4174) can switch between two local releases and simulate failed asset downloads or unavailable game network routes without writing production scores. It creates disposable files under `.private/update-lab` and uses that local origin's browser storage. The [October 14 review](audit/2026-10-14-paddle-update.md) records the collision fix and update verification.

Updates also appear in a sticky notice above the start-screen arena and in **Settings → Game updates**, which offers **Check for updates**. Visible connected pages check every minute; the pause menu announces a downloaded update. A closed app may activate an update before its next launch, so an already-current launch has no update button. See [the update visibility investigation](UPDATE-VISIBILITY-INVESTIGATION.md) for the discovered placement and detection gaps and their corrections.

Browser storage can be cleared or evicted under storage pressure. The install action requests persistent storage where supported, but the browser decides whether to grant it. A new browser or cleared installation must download the game again; unsent scores and local progress are lost if their storage is removed. Sync runs while the game is open; it does not depend on, or promise, background submission after the app closes.

See [PWA-UPGRADE.md](PWA-UPGRADE.md) for release integrity, queue behavior, optimization details and validation limits.

The [PWA robustness review](PWA-ROBUSTNESS-REVIEW.md) records the October 15 cache-loss, update, installation and queue audit, primary browser guidance, 125 passing automated tests and isolated browser evidence. Readiness now checks the asset inventory; release pins survive asset eviction; network downloads have deadlines; stale repair replies cannot replace newer state; and explicit retries use actual network results. The review records the subsequent verified publication and lists physical-device checks still needed.

## Scoring

| Award | Calculation |
| --- | --- |
| Destroyed brick | `100 × min(5, 1 + floor(combo / 6))`; combo increments before the award |
| Collected falling power-up | 150 points, independent of the combo |
| Normal board clear | `750 + 150 × lives remaining` |
| First two Citadel / Nexus formations | 500 clear points each |
| Speed bonus per cleared board / formation | `max(0, 2,000 − 10 × floor(active board seconds))` |
| Milestone extra life | Every 12,000 points, up to nine lives; no pickup points |

Any ball contacting the paddle resets the shared combo. Ready-to-launch time, pauses and cutscenes are excluded from active time; holding a sticky ball during play counts. Life loss preserves the board timer. Personal best combines Adventure and Daily Challenge; saving a named shared score is a separate action.

See [SCORING.md](SCORING.md) for streak examples, power-up durations, timing rules and difficulty changes.

## Run locally

Use Bun 1.4.3 or newer (1.4.3 was verified for this tooling):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/pagelove/prism-breaker.git
cd prism-breaker
bun tools/serve.mjs
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:4173**. No dependency install or build is required to serve the committed release. After changing runtime files, rebuild the offline release with `bun tools/build-pwa.mjs` before reviewing it in a controlled browser tab.

It does not emulate Pagelove's score writes or rule enforcement. `public/scores.html` is an empty template, so local play has no live community scores. ## Deployment and maintenance

The publisher in `tools/remote.mjs` pins:

- Public game: `https://sane-guild-8399.onpagelove.com/`
- Owner authoring endpoint: `https://dav-sane-guild-8399.onpagelove.com/`

Publishing requires the host owner's credential. Start `bun tools/remote.mjs` in an interactive terminal and wait for **Ready for hidden JSON input**. Authenticate through the publisher's hidden stdin `auth` operation. Keep the key out of command arguments, environment variables, files, source control and browser code. The publisher keeps it in process memory and checks that the authorized console identifies the expected DAV host.

After all runtime and asset edits, generate and check the offline release:

```sh
bun run build
bun tools/build-pwa.mjs --check
```

Commit the exact source, then run `bun run release:check` before publishing. This runs the behavioral suite, PWA consistency, maintained document links, local module imports and a limited credential-pattern check. Its ignored evidence names the source commit, content digest and runtime release and lasts 24 hours. The publisher rejects missing/stale evidence and dirty release inputs; it checks again before uploading the worker. Recheck after source/documentation edits or a new commit. This gate does not certify physical devices or unresolved platform contracts.

Run publishing checks from the actual Git checkout of `pagelove/prism-breaker`. A separate authoring mirror or a folder inside an unrelated parent repository cannot issue release approval. It can still build, run tests and preview the game.

The pinned [Quality workflow](.github/workflows/quality.yml) installs frozen Bun dependencies, regenerates artifacts, rejects generated drift and runs the gate on pushes and pull requests. See [review results](FOLLOW-UP-REVIEW-RESULTS.md) for actual hosted-check/branch-protection status. Run repository checks separately with `bun run check:repository`.

The builder derives a release identity from runtime assets, composition inputs, the worker and packaging code. It generates the source marker/module/worker and an ignored immutable package under `test-results/release-package/<release-id>/`. Published HTML references that package, while native worlds and scores retain their original resources. See [immutable publication and rollback](RELEASE-PUBLICATION.md).

After authentication, normal publishing uses `{"op":"deploy"}`; exit with `{"op":"quit"}`. Normal deployment:

1. Stages and verifies create-only files under `/releases/<release-id>/`, then conditionally promotes self-contained entry documents, with root `sw.js` last. Legacy root scripts/styles remain unchanged for older visitors.
2. **Excludes `scores.html` and all `worlds/*/definition.html` data**, preserving community scores, rules and edited worlds. Native editor routes are stored at `/editor/:worldname`; `seedWorlds` creates only missing world resources.
3. Verifies binary/text bytes and normalized HTML structure, refusing collisions or concurrent entry edits. The worker downloads immutable URLs into logical release caches.
4. Writes a non-secret release receipt to ignored `deployment.json`.

Game publication rejects `initializeScores` and never writes score policies or records. `migrateScoreRules` permits record-preserving maintenance only when native policy identity is unchanged; changed rules are refused until a supported safe activation procedure is established. Fresh-host policy setup requires a separate reviewed procedure. The known propagation issue is not declared solved by warming a few requests. See [native platform requirements](PLATFORM-REQUIREMENTS.md).

When switching hosts, update the publisher, the pinned absolute-asset origin in `tools/immutable-release.mjs`, entry-page canonical/social URLs, score type/schema, score grammar and `tools/build-data.mjs` together. Vocabulary IRIs such as `https://pagelove.org/Schema` identify platform rule types; they are separate from the game host and Pagelove website link.

Private backups, credentials, live score exports, generated preview files and deployment receipts are excluded from Git. The public score template stays empty. Keep import/entry-page version parameters current for browsers without an active worker, then regenerate the offline release. A complete release cache resolves runtime URLs by path so query variants use the same release's asset.

### Operational limits

- Gameplay requires WebGL 2 support. Reduced effects lowers rendering cost, but smoothness and audio behavior vary across hardware and browser settings.
- Native share destinations and their handling of text/files are controlled by the browser, OS and receiving app. Copy invitation and download remain fallbacks. Physical Android-to-Slack delivery is not established by desktop preview review.
- Progress and preferences use browser storage; clearing that storage removes them. The game has no accounts or cloud progress synchronization.
- Fresh score reads and publishing queued scores require the Pagelove host. Offline standings remain a dated snapshot; queued scores sync when connectivity returns and the game is open.
- Physical Android installation, airplane-mode relaunch, and updates between two installed production releases still require device verification. Local browser checks do not establish those results.
